rationale:
Split into two new lemmas plus two reused accepted declarations. The supplied proof has two independent analytic ingredients, joined by Lebesgue's differentiation theorem:
(i) The slice bound at a differentiability point of a distribution function (steps 1–3). The proof applies it twice, to μ and to μ'.
(ii) A Markov/Chebyshev choice of a point of (ρ/2, ρ), off a null set, where ofReal(F′) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ)·B (steps 5–6).
Each is a self-contained, reusable statement, and each rests on a different accepted declaration: (i) on cbr_smm_liminf_left_slope_le_deriv, and (ii) on cmcs_smi_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le, which is already the selected node's resolved dependency. Both are reused with byte-identical frozen types. Leaf proofs may not add helper declarations, so this factoring is the clean way to use them.

slice_liminf is stated for an arbitrary measurable space α, because the argument never uses ℝ^P. This makes it more reusable. It also keeps both new child types free of GMT.Ch07.Euclid, which the flow's speculative stub module (runtime._install_speculative_assumptions, emitted outside namespace GMT.Ch07) cannot resolve. Checked: the Euclid form fails there with "Unknown identifier `Euclid`", and the generalized form elaborates.

Parent assembly (steps 1, 4, 5b and 6 of the supplied proof; no child proves this part):
1. Given P, μ, μ', f, ρ, B and the hypotheses, put F(s) := (μ{f < s}).toReal and G(s) := (μ'{f < s}).toReal. Both are monotone (measure_mono, ENNReal.toReal_mono, measure_ne_top).
2. N := {t | ¬DifferentiableAt ℝ F t} ∪ {t | ¬DifferentiableAt ℝ G t} has volume 0 (Monotone.ae_differentiableAt, ae_iff, measure_union_null).
3. Since F(ρ/2) ≥ 0, ofReal(F ρ − F(ρ/2)) ≤ ofReal(F ρ) = μ{f < ρ} ≤ B.
4. markov_point applied to (F, ρ, B, N) gives r ∈ Ioo (ρ/2) ρ with r ∉ N and ofReal(deriv F r) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ)·B.
5. Since r ∉ N, both F and G are differentiable at r.
6. slice_liminf with α = Euclid P, applied to μ, gives liminf ≤ ofReal(deriv F r) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ)·B.
7. Applied to μ', it gives liminf ≤ ofReal(deriv G r) < ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top).

subproblems.title: Left slice density bounded by the derivative of the distribution function, for a finite measure on any measurable space (Simon 6.4.9–4.10, used in 6.5.1 (10))
subproblems.statement: Let α be a measurable space (a type α : Type with a σ-algebra, given by the instance [MeasurableSpace α]), let μ be a finite measure on α (IsFiniteMeasure μ), let f : α → ℝ be measurable and let t ∈ ℝ. Put F(s) := (μ({x ∈ α : f(x) < s})).toReal for s ∈ ℝ, the distribution function of f under μ, read in ℝ. If F is differentiable at t, then liminf_{h → 0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({x : t − h < f(x) < t}) ≤ ofReal(F′(t)). Here F′ = deriv F, ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, values lie in [0, ∞], and the liminf is taken along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 of right neighbourhoods of 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (α : Type) [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α) (f : α → ℝ) (t : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasure μ → Measurable f → DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s : ℝ => (μ {x | f x < s}).toReal) t → liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t}) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (deriv (fun s : ℝ => (μ {x | f x < s}).toReal) t)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–3 of the parent's supplied proof of cmcsd_good_radius, for one finite measure. The argument never uses the structure of ℝ^P, so it is stated for an arbitrary measurable space α; the parent applies it with α = ℝ^P (Euclid P), once to μ and once to μ'. The book source is Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6. The remark after 4.9 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1361–1375) says t ↦ M_W(T⌞{f < t}) is increasing, hence differentiable L¹-a.e., and slice masses are controlled by liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹·M(T⌞{t − h < f < t}). The proof of 5.1, (8)–(10) (lines 1725–1734) uses this to choose the slicing radius. Throughout, ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal, A_s := {x ∈ α : f(x) < s} for s ∈ ℝ, and F(s) := (μ(A_s)).toReal. So F is exactly the function fun s : ℝ => (μ {x | f x < s}).toReal of the statement, and the hypothesis says F is differentiable at t.

1. (Finite values of the distribution function.) For each s ∈ ℝ the set A_s is measurable, because f and the constant s are measurable (measurableSet_lt hf measurable_const). Since μ is a finite measure, μ(A_s) ≠ ∞ (measure_ne_top). Hence μ(A_s) = ofReal(F(s)) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal) and F(s) ≥ 0 (ENNReal.toReal_nonneg).

2. (Slice bound.) Fix h > 0. Since t − h < t, A_{t−h} ⊆ A_t. If t − h < f(x) < t, then x ∈ A_t and x ∉ A_{t−h}, because f(x) < t − h would contradict t − h < f(x). Hence {x : t − h < f(x) < t} ⊆ A_t \ A_{t−h}. Apply monotonicity of μ (measure_mono) and measure_sdiff. The latter applies because A_{t−h} ⊆ A_t, A_{t−h} is measurable (hence null-measurable), and μ(A_{t−h}) ≠ ∞. This gives
   μ({t − h < f < t}) ≤ μ(A_t \ A_{t−h}) = μ(A_t) − μ(A_{t−h}) = ofReal(F(t)) − ofReal(F(t − h)) = ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)).
   The last two equalities use step 1 and ENNReal.ofReal_sub, which is valid because F(t − h) ≥ 0. Multiplying both sides by ofReal(h⁻¹) preserves the inequality in [0, ∞] (monotonicity of multiplication, e.g. gcongr). So for every h > 0,
   ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({t − h < f < t}) ≤ ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)).

3. (Comparison of the liminfs.) The set (0, ∞) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin), so the inequality of step 2 holds eventually along 𝓝[>] 0. In the complete lattice [0, ∞], liminf is monotone under eventual inequality, with no boundedness side conditions (Filter.liminf_le_liminf; its boundedness arguments are discharged automatically in a complete lattice). Hence
   liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({t − h < f < t}) ≤ liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)).

4. (Left slopes at a point of differentiability.) F is differentiable at t by hypothesis. The sibling cbr_smm_liminf_left_slope_le_deriv, applied to F and t, gives
   liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) ≤ ofReal(deriv F t).
   This is step 3 of the parent's proof: the left quotients h⁻¹(F(t) − F(t − h)) tend to F′(t) as h ↓ 0, and for h > 0 the product equals ofReal(h⁻¹(F(t) − F(t − h))), which tends to ofReal(F′(t)).

5. (Conclusion.) Chaining steps 3 and 4 gives liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({x : t − h < f(x) < t}) ≤ ofReal(deriv F t). This is the claim, because F is literally fun s : ℝ => (μ {x | f x < s}).toReal. ∎
proof_key_steps: A_s := {f < s} is measurable and μ(A_s) = ofReal(F(s)) with F(s) = (μ A_s).toReal ≥ 0 (finite measure).
For h > 0: {t − h < f < t} ⊆ A_t \ A_{t−h}, so μ({t − h < f < t}) ≤ μ(A_t) − μ(A_{t−h}) = ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) (measure_sdiff, ENNReal.ofReal_sub); multiply by ofReal(h⁻¹).
The bound holds eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, so the liminfs compare (Filter.liminf_le_liminf in [0, ∞]).
The sibling cbr_smm_liminf_left_slope_le_deriv bounds liminf ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) by ofReal(deriv F t).

subproblems.title: Markov choice of r ∈ (ρ/2, ρ) off a null set with ofReal(F′(r)) ≤ (4/ρ)·B (Simon 6.5.1 (10))
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ → ℝ be monotone (nondecreasing), let ρ > 0 be real, let B ∈ [0, ∞], and let N ⊆ ℝ be Lebesgue-null (volume N = 0). Suppose ofReal(F(ρ) − F(ρ/2)) ≤ B. Then there is r with ρ/2 < r < ρ and r ∉ N such that ofReal(F′(r)) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ)·B. Here F′ = deriv F (Mathlib's derivative, equal to 0 where F is not differentiable), ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, and the product is taken in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (F : ℝ → ℝ) (ρ : ℝ) (B : ℝ≥0∞) (N : Set ℝ), Monotone F → 0 < ρ → ENNReal.ofReal (F ρ - F (ρ / 2)) ≤ B → (volume : Measure ℝ) N = 0 → ∃ r ∈ Ioo (ρ / 2) ρ, r ∉ N ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (deriv F r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (4 / ρ) * B
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–6 of the parent's supplied proof of cmcsd_good_radius, isolated for a general monotone F and an arbitrary Lebesgue-null set N. The book source is Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, (10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1731–1734): "by 4.10 we know that for each ρ ∈ (0, 1/4) we can find σ ∈ (ρ/2, ρ) such that M⟨T_ρ, d, σ⟩ ≤ (c/ρ)·M(T_ρ − T_{ρ/2})". The integral bound behind it is the remark before 4.10 (lines 1367–1375). Markov's inequality is the measure-theoretic one (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov%27s_inequality). Throughout, ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal, λ := volume (Lebesgue measure on ℝ), F′ := deriv F, and
   I := Ioo (ρ/2) ρ, c := ofReal(4/ρ)·B ∈ [0, ∞], g(t) := ofReal(F′(t)), S := {t ∈ I : g(t) ≤ c}.

1. (The interval.) I is measurable (measurableSet_Ioo), and λ(I) = ofReal(ρ − ρ/2) = ofReal(ρ/2) (Real.volume_Ioo). Since ρ > 0, we have ρ/2 > 0 and so λ(I) > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos). Also 4/ρ > 0, so ofReal(4/ρ) > 0.

2. (Integral bound.) g is measurable: deriv F is measurable (measurable_deriv), and so is its composition with ENNReal.ofReal (Measurable.ennreal_ofReal). Apply the sibling cmcs_smi_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le with a = ρ/2 and b = ρ (F is monotone). It gives ∫⁻_I g dλ ≤ ofReal(F(ρ) − F(ρ/2)), and this is ≤ B by hypothesis. So ∫⁻_I g dλ ≤ B.

3. (Covering inequality.) Every t ∈ I lies in S or in I \ S, so I ⊆ S ∪ (I \ S). Hence λ(I) ≤ λ(S ∪ (I \ S)) ≤ λ(S) + λ(I \ S) (measure_mono, measure_union_le).

4. (λ(S) > 0.) There are three cases.
   (a) B = ∞. Then c = ofReal(4/ρ)·∞ = ∞, because ofReal(4/ρ) ≠ 0 (ENNReal.mul_top). Every t ∈ I satisfies g(t) ≤ ∞ = c. So S = I, and λ(S) = λ(I) > 0 by step 1.
   (b) B = 0. Then c = ofReal(4/ρ)·0 = 0. By step 2, ∫⁻_I g dλ ≤ 0, so ∫⁻_I g dλ = 0. Since g is measurable, lintegral_eq_zero_iff gives g = 0 almost everywhere for λ⌞I = volume.restrict I. That is, λ⌞I({t : g(t) ≠ 0}) = 0 (ae_iff), i.e. λ({t : g(t) ≠ 0} ∩ I) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply' with I measurable). If t ∈ I \ S, then g(t) ≤ 0 = c fails, so g(t) ≠ 0. Thus I \ S ⊆ {t : g(t) ≠ 0} ∩ I, and λ(I \ S) = 0 (measure_mono_null). Step 3 then gives λ(I) ≤ λ(S) + 0, so λ(S) ≥ λ(I) > 0.
   (c) 0 < B < ∞. Apply Markov's inequality to the measure λ⌞I and the measurable function g (mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀): c·λ⌞I({t : c ≤ g(t)}) ≤ ∫⁻_I g dλ. Put E := {t : c ≤ g(t)} ∩ I; then λ⌞I({c ≤ g}) = λ(E) (Measure.restrict_apply'). With step 2, c·λ(E) ≤ B. By commutativity and associativity, c·λ(E) = B·(ofReal(4/ρ)·λ(E)), so B·(ofReal(4/ρ)·λ(E)) ≤ B·1. Since B ≠ 0 and B ≠ ∞, B cancels (ENNReal.mul_le_mul_iff_right): ofReal(4/ρ)·λ(E) ≤ 1. Hence λ(E) ≤ (ofReal(4/ρ))⁻¹ (ENNReal.le_inv_iff_mul_le). Moreover (ofReal(4/ρ))⁻¹ = ofReal((4/ρ)⁻¹) = ofReal(ρ/4) (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos with 4/ρ > 0; inv_div). If t ∈ I \ S, then g(t) ≤ c fails, so c < g(t); in particular c ≤ g(t) and t ∈ E. Hence I \ S ⊆ E and λ(I \ S) ≤ λ(E) ≤ ofReal(ρ/4). Now suppose, for contradiction, that λ(S) = 0. Step 3 gives ofReal(ρ/2) = λ(I) ≤ 0 + ofReal(ρ/4) = ofReal(ρ/4). Since ρ/4 ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff gives ρ/2 ≤ ρ/4, contradicting ρ > 0. Hence λ(S) > 0.

5. (Avoiding the null set.) Since λ(N) = 0, λ(S \ N) = λ(S) (measure_sdiff_null), and this is > 0 by step 4. A set of nonzero measure is nonempty (nonempty_of_measure_ne_zero), so there is r ∈ S \ N.

6. (Conclusion.) For this r: r ∈ S ⊆ I, so ρ/2 < r < ρ. Also r ∉ N, and ofReal(deriv F r) = g(r) ≤ c = ofReal(4/ρ)·B by definition of S. ∎
proof_key_steps: I := (ρ/2, ρ) has λ(I) = ofReal(ρ/2) > 0; g := ofReal ∘ deriv F is measurable; c := ofReal(4/ρ)·B; S := {t ∈ I : g t ≤ c}.
∫⁻_I g ≤ ofReal(F(ρ) − F(ρ/2)) ≤ B by the sibling cmcs_smi_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le and the hypothesis.
λ(S) > 0: if B = ∞ then c = ∞ and S = I; if B = 0 then g = 0 a.e. on I, so I \ S is null; if 0 < B < ∞ then Markov gives λ(I \ S) ≤ ofReal(ρ/4) < ofReal(ρ/2) = λ(I).
λ(S \ N) = λ(S) > 0, so pick r ∈ S \ N.

subproblems.title: Lebesgue's inequality ∫_a^b F′ ≤ F(b) − F(a) for monotone F, lower-integral form (reuse of the accepted declaration cmcs_smi_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le)
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ → ℝ be monotone (nondecreasing), let a, b ∈ ℝ, and let F′ := deriv F (Mathlib's derivative, equal to 0 at points where F is not differentiable). Then the lower Lebesgue integral over (a, b) with respect to Lebesgue measure satisfies ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(F′(t)) dt ≤ ofReal(F(b) − F(a)), where ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is ENNReal.ofReal. This is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmcs_smi_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le, reused with its identical frozen Lean type.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (F : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ), Monotone F → ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, ENNReal.ofReal (deriv F t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (F b - F a)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note: this is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmcs_smi_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le. Its node is root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.slicing-a1.mass_integral-a1.lebesgue_deriv-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 6efe397f182ee5f93e5be9c4b09eb298c3f56ad8), and it is already the resolved dependency of the selected node. Its accepted Lean proof recompiles in this session (Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c) with axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only, and needs no import beyond the frozen Submission header. The argument below is the import-free Stieltjes route of that accepted proof.

Provenance: Simon Ch. 6, remark before 4.10 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1367–1372): an increasing function of t is differentiable L¹-a.e. and the integral of its derivative over (a, b) is at most its increment. This is Lebesgue's theorem for monotone functions; see B. Forrest, Differentiation of Monotone Functions, PMath 451 slides, https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/~beforres/PMath451/Lectures/Chapter5/Differentiate/DifferentiateSlides.pdf. Notation: ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal, λ := volume, F′ := deriv F (Mathlib's derivative, 0 where F is not differentiable).

1. (Stieltjes modification.) Let G := hF.stieltjesFunction (Monotone.stieltjesFunction), the monotone right-continuous function G(x) = F(x⁺) = rightLim F x, and let μ_G := G.measure be its Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure. Then μ_G((a, b)) = ofReal(G(b⁻) − G(a)), with G(b⁻) := leftLim G b (StieltjesFunction.measure_Ioo).

2. (Endpoint comparison.) F(a) ≤ G(a) (Monotone.le_rightLim with a ≤ a). For y < b, G(y) = F(y⁺) ≤ F(b) (Monotone.rightLim_le). Also G(y) → G(b⁻) as y ↑ b (Monotone.tendsto_leftLim along 𝓝[<] b), and (−∞, b) ∈ 𝓝[<] b (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Hence G(b⁻) ≤ F(b) (le_of_tendsto). Consequently G(b⁻) − G(a) ≤ F(b) − F(a).

3. (Lebesgue differentiation.) By Monotone.ae_hasDerivAt, for λ-a.e. t, F has derivative (μ_G.rnDeriv λ t).toReal at t. At such t, deriv F t = (μ_G.rnDeriv λ t).toReal (HasDerivAt.deriv). Hence ofReal(deriv F t) = ofReal((μ_G.rnDeriv λ t).toReal) ≤ μ_G.rnDeriv λ t (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le).

4. (Integration.) Step 3 holds λ⌞(a, b)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae). So
   ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(F′) dλ ≤ ∫⁻_{(a,b)} μ_G.rnDeriv λ dλ (lintegral_mono_ae)
   ≤ (λ.withDensity (μ_G.rnDeriv λ))((a, b)) (withDensity_apply_le)
   ≤ μ_G((a, b)) (Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_le)
   = ofReal(G(b⁻) − G(a)) (step 1)
   ≤ ofReal(F(b) − F(a)) (step 2 and ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reuse of the accepted declaration cmcs_smi_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le (identical type).
G := F(·⁺) is a Stieltjes function with μ_G((a, b)) = ofReal(G(b⁻) − G(a)) ≤ ofReal(F(b) − F(a)).

subproblems.title: Left difference quotients in [0, ∞] at a point of differentiability (reuse of the accepted declaration cbr_smm_liminf_left_slope_le_deriv)
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ → ℝ be differentiable at t ∈ ℝ. Then liminf_{h→0⁺} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·ENNReal.ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(F′(t)), with the liminf taken along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 and F′ = deriv F. This is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cbr_smm_liminf_left_slope_le_deriv, reused with its identical frozen Lean type.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (F : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ), DifferentiableAt ℝ F t → liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * ENNReal.ofReal (F t - F (t - h))) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (deriv F t)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note: this is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cbr_smm_liminf_left_slope_le_deriv. Its node is root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.convergence_tools-a1.slice_majorant-a1.left_slope-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 9e4623f7949b6e8a31421369c9b6bcbc190d2c41). Its accepted Lean proof recompiles in this session (Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c) with axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only, and needs no import beyond the frozen Submission header. The accepted, reviewed natural-language proof of that node is reproduced below. It is also step 3 of the parent's supplied proof of cmcsd_good_radius.

Provenance: the pointwise step behind 4.9 and "M(∂(T⌞B_r(ξ))) ≤ f′(r) for L¹-a.e. r" in Simon's proof of Ch. 6, 8.2 (2) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 2345–2347). Monotonicity of F is not needed. Write D := deriv F t and ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal.

1. Since F is differentiable at t, F has derivative D at t (DifferentiableAt.hasDerivAt).

2. (Left difference quotients.) By HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_left, s⁻¹·(F(t + s) − F(t)) → D as s → 0 along 𝓝[<] 0. The map h ↦ −h sends 𝓝[>] 0 into 𝓝[<] 0 (tendsto_neg_nhdsGT at a = 0, simplifying −0 = 0). Composing the two limits, (−h)⁻¹·(F(t + (−h)) − F(t)) → D as h → 0⁺. For every real h, (−h)⁻¹·(F(t − h) − F(t)) = −h⁻¹·(F(t − h) − F(t)) = h⁻¹·(F(t) − F(t − h)) (inv_neg, ring). Hence q(h) := h⁻¹·(F(t) − F(t − h)) → D along 𝓝[>] 0.

3. (Passing to [0, ∞].) Since ofReal is continuous, ofReal(q(h)) → ofReal(D) along 𝓝[>] 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal). For h > 0 we have h⁻¹ ≥ 0, so ENNReal.ofReal_mul gives ofReal(q(h)) = ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)). The set (0, ∞) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). So φ(h) := ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) agrees with ofReal(q(h)) eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, and therefore φ(h) → ofReal(D) along 𝓝[>] 0 (Tendsto.congr').

4. (Conclusion.) The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial, and [0, ∞] is a complete linear order with the order topology. So the liminf of a convergent function equals its limit (Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq), and liminf_{h→0⁺} φ(h) = ofReal(D). In particular liminf_{h→0⁺} φ(h) ≤ ofReal(deriv F t). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reuse of the accepted declaration cbr_smm_liminf_left_slope_le_deriv (identical type).
HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_left composed with h ↦ −h (tendsto_neg_nhdsGT) gives h⁻¹(F(t) − F(t − h)) → deriv F t along 𝓝[>] 0.
For h > 0, ofReal(h⁻¹)·ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) = ofReal(h⁻¹(F(t) − F(t − h))) → ofReal(deriv F t) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal).
On the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>] 0 the liminf of a convergent function equals its limit (Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq).
